[0] everyday_reading (E): In geometry a point has no size, and on screens positions are pixels with y pointing down. StdDraw.point(x, y) draws a visible spot (a circle of the pen radius) in user coordinates: the default is the unit square, with (0, 0) at the lower-left corner.
[1] misconception (M) -> PixelCoordinates: wrong rule: StdDraw.point(256, 256) draws in the middle of the default window. Right rule: The default window is 512-by-512 pixels, but coordinates are in the unit square, so the middle is (0.5, 0.5). (256, 256) is far off the canvas.
[2] inconsistent_trace (T) -> PixelCoordinates: Points to LT (commands run in program order; each uses the current scale, color and pen radius; later marks cover earlier ones). An uneven trace uses pixel units for some points, puts y downwards, or applies a setting to commands issued before it. (here mixing in: "StdDraw.point(256, 256) draws in the middle of the default window")
[3] misconception (M) -> DrawWithoutShow: wrong rule: With double buffering on, each drawing command appears on screen immediately. Right rule: By default each command is shown at once. After StdDraw.show(t) turns animation mode on, drawing is collected off-screen and appears only at the next show(t). show() with no argument turns per-command display back on. (Newer StdDraw versions use enableDoubleBuffering().)

[0] names_the_element (N): StdDraw is a booksite library of static methods for graphical output: lines, points, shapes and text drawn on a 2-D canvas in a window.
[1] states_the_rule (S): StdDraw models an abstract device that draws lines and points on a two-dimensional canvas. The default scale is the unit square, and methods with no arguments reset to the defaults.

[0] line_by_line_trace (LT): Calls run in program order. Each control command (setXscale, setPenRadius, setPenColor) affects only the drawing commands after it, and each drawing command paints over what is already on the canvas.
[1] output_prediction (OP): The result is a picture in a window, not a value: the methods are void. Triangle's three line() calls and one point() call produce an equilateral triangle with a dot inside.
[2] one_step_execution (OS): One drawing command adds marks to the canvas (shown at once by default). One control command changes the drawing state (scale, pen radius or color) without drawing anything.

[0] relation_to_neighbour (R): StdIn values can be drawn directly: PlotFilter reads the bounding box, then point coordinates, and calls StdDraw.point for each pair. Both libraries must be downloaded into the program's directory.
[1] relation_to_neighbour (R): StdOut writes text to a stream, while StdDraw draws in a separate window at (x, y) coordinates. Neither affects the other.
[2] relation_to_neighbour (R): Animation reuses StdDraw's drawing commands but adds clear() and show(t), which control when the canvas is erased and displayed.
[3] relation_to_neighbour (R): setXscale and setYscale set the coordinate system that every later StdDraw command uses.
[4] relation_to_neighbour (R): Shape commands are StdDraw drawing commands. They use the same coordinates, pen color and pen radius as line and point.
[5] purpose_of_the_whole (P): StdDraw is used to visualize data and functions, which is often more meaningful than lists of numbers.

[0] predict_a_change (C) -> PixelCoordinates: Rescaling the coordinates together with the data keeps the picture. The pen radius is not affected by scaling. Reordering drawing commands changes which mark covers which.
[1] transfer_to_a_new_program (X): Use StdDraw for simple plots, data visualizations and teaching animations. It is crude compared with production graphics libraries, and exact numeric results belong on standard output.
[2] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: StdDraw.java must be in the working directory or on the classpath. Kind: run-time exception. Trigger class: Running without StdDraw.class available: NoClassDefFoundError: StdDraw (javac reports 'cannot find symbol' if it is missing at compile time).
[3] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: Coordinates must lie inside the current scale to be visible. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: Pixel-style coordinates such as (256, 256) with the default unit square: nothing visible is drawn.
[4] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: setCanvasSize must be called before any drawing. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: Calling setCanvasSize() after drawing commands, so the earlier drawing is lost.

Like StdIn, StdDraw is a library downloaded from the booksite; StdIn brings values into the program, while StdDraw produces drawings as output.
StdOut writes text to the output stream; StdDraw draws shapes at (x, y) coordinates in a window.
StdDraw is a library used through its API of static methods.
Animation uses StdDraw's clear() and show() methods to make dynamic changes to the image on the screen.
Scaling sets the coordinate system StdDraw uses.
Shape commands are StdDraw drawing commands.
A function is plotted by drawing its sampled points and lines with StdDraw.
Mouse position and clicks are read through StdDraw methods such as StdDraw.mousePressed().
